name: GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program
summary: Global GEF and IUCN programme giving larger grants to civil society organisations that scale or replicate proven environmental solutions, including community-based management of threatened ecosystems and species, through regional calls.

eligibility.rule: Have a legal entity and a bank account in the organisation's name
Be authorised to receive foreign charitable contributions and directly implement the project
Base the proposal on existing work with high potential for impact and scalability
Not be a government body receiving grant funding directly
Have no relationship that could create a conflict of interest
Not be a current IUCN or GEF employee or immediate family member
Exclude third-party sub-grants, pure research and conservation planning
Submit no more than two proposals as lead partner and receive no more than one grant

documents: Articles of incorporation, constitution, statutes, government decree, registration certificate or bylaws

calls.label: 2026 regional calls for proposals
calls.note: Deadlines are announced at the launch of each regional call

status.quote: The deadlines for each regional Call for Proposal will be announced at their official launch.

administered_by.quote: IUCN and the Global Environment Facility (GEF) welcome submission of proposals to the GEF Small Grants Program CSO Challenge Program

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants are local, national, regional, or international civil society organizations (CSOs)

geography.quote: Projects must be implemented in GEF SGP-eligible recipient countries

access.quote: Applications can be submitted https://csochallenge.org/. only through the program website

window.quote: The deadlines for each regional Call for Proposal will be announced at their official launch.

amount.quote: The program provides grant funding of up to $300,000 USD

co_finance_required.quote: Co-funding is not required but is strongly encouraged and strengthens the proposal.

consortium_required.quote: The lead partner may apply alone or with co-applicants.

effort.quote: Proposals (Concept Notes) will be shortlisted based on the evaluation by a Selection Committee.
Shortlisted applicants will be asked to develop Full Proposals.

eligibility.quote: Proponents must be Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) with legal entity and a bank account in the name of the organization

Eligible applicants are local, national, regional, or international civil society organizations (CSOs) that are authorized to receive charitable contributions from foreign sources, maintain a bank account in the organization's name, and are directly responsible for implementing the project.
be based on existing work with high potential for impact and scalability (not just a concept)
Governments may participate in project activities but are not eligible to receive grant funding directly.
Applicants must not have any personal, financial, political, or other relationship that could create a conflict of interest in relation to this funding opportunity.
Current employees of IUCN or the GEF, and their immediate family members, are not eligible to apply.
In addition, financial support to third parties through sub-grants and pure research or conservation planning are ineligible.

An applicant may submit a maximum of two proposals as lead partner and may be a co-applicant in any number of applications but may receive only one grant; if both proposals score highly, only the higher-scoring one is selected.

documents.quote: Articles of Incorporation, Constitution, Statutes, Government Decree, as appropriate (certificate of registration or bylaws) Organization in-country registration certificate (if applicable)
